notes.title: Developers diaries #5
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e3f49b0636b4b6868cbe962c4313f325cebac9bd.png[/img]

[h3]How a Gas Station Works[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/1ad9b0993429e0b2fa5de3dfd73433b2e99d3bf6.png[/img]

The player arrives at the gas station, drives up to the gas station they need, depending on the type of fuel and the side of the fuel tank hatch, the Overlap event is triggered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f90dc83b97096546ef4e7365b8192a7bb4a3eca0.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]OnComponentBeginOverlap [/b]event is called when the player hits the trigger of the refueling column, further logic is triggered.
[*] The [b]CarTagsRefuel [/b]macro receives data from the car, what type of fuel it has, and on which side it has a fuel tank hatch.
[*] The [b]DataRefuelColumn [/b]macro receives data from the CarTagsRefuel macro and compares it with the specified parameters of the refueling column.
[*] The [b]SendingDataGasStation [/b]function generates and sends all the data to the refueling logic.
[*] After the data is generated, the refueling script is initialized.
[/list]
The script initialization has passed and the script has subscribed to the [b]RefuelStatus [/b]event via the [b]BindEvent [/b]to [b]RefuelStatus [/b]node. Now, when this event is called from anywhere else, the event in our script will trigger. This is called [b]Event Dispatcher[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/ce64f41974074d3728b5d493e9d54c3884365de8.png[/img]
[list]
[*] As soon as the event to which the script is subscribed is triggered, the [b]Refuel [/b]post-event is called and the chain of checks is started.
[*] First, the status of the [b]RefuelButtonHovered [/b]variable is checked (whether the button is pressed or not) via the [b]Branch [/b]node. This node checks whether the value being checked satisfies any specified conditions; in this case, it is checked whether the value of the [b]RefuelButtonHovered [/b]variable is TRUE or FALSE. If the button is pressed, the check is successful because the variable returns True, and the chain continues.
[/list]
Check is carried out via the CheckStatusCar macro, inside which the following is checked:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/438f4e157d009f5ca9000de364a3d3000c23bcd2.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The first two [b]Branch [/b]nodes check whether the engine is turned off and whether the parking brake is activated. If this check is passed, the macro proceeds the script’s progress further.
[*] If the conditions are not met, the macro simply waits for the actions to be performed via the [b]Delay [/b]node (time delay node).
[/list]
Next comes the check and execution of actions via the TankFilling macro, inside which the following is checked:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/9698044879de8a0d721fb3ff012a7e87c25e7c13.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The refueling confirmation variable is initialized and set to [b]False[/b]. At this stage, our script is already ready to complete refueling.
[*] After that, the current fuel level is recorded in the [b]BackupFuelLevel [/b]variable and stored there until the end of refueling.
[*] In the [b]FuelLevelConverted [/b]variable, the tank filling level was previously formed into a decimal structure, i.e. the tank level is measured not in liters, but in fractions from 0 to 1. After that, via the [b]Branch [/b]node, it is checked whether the tank has filled up to 1.
[*] Next, the script checks via the [b]Branch [/b]node again whether the refueling button is still pressed.
[/list]
After the previous checks, a number of execution units are launched, in which pure mathematical operations occur with a calculation interval equal to 0.1 seconds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/53925c561f32df0026dda82dac3fe8a326ad89a7.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]AddLitreInProgressBar [/b]unit animates the filling level of the tank inside the Refueling button. The current tank filling level value is summed up with the fuel supply flowrate.
[*] The [b]DisplayFuelLitre [/b]unit sends the amount of refueled fuel to the user interface.
[*] The [b]AddFuelInCar [/b]unit adds fuel to the vehicle’s tank. Every 0.1 seconds, 0.1 liters of fuel is sent to the tank level value.
[*] The [b]FilledFuel [/b]unit calculates how much fuel the player has filled into the tank. The value of the previously set [b]BackupFuelLevel [/b]variable is subtracted from the current tank filling level.
[*] The [b]SumLitre [/b]unit generates and distributes refueling data, sends data to the refueling logic and to the logic of the car.
[/list]
As soon as the player releases the refueling button, they have the opportunity to complete the refueling process and confirm the amount of refueled fuel. When the completion button is pressed, the confirmation logic is executed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/fb8eb29a569a6bdf76cf878d8a37f61cdce19fe4.png[/img]
[list]
[*] A new tank level value is written to the previously set BackupFuelLevel variable.
[*] The user interface closes.
[*] A user message about successful refueling is issued.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/db5fb7eb8ff88d20db5c7f397780430f48d9cf5f.gif[/img]



[h3]How a Repair Station Works[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/b13286eaaa31cd602b2520956794f745527d76bd.png[/img]

When a player enters the Service Station zone, the Service Station logic script is initialized.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/abca19f178e4b1b7e902dfa20633123518c1f656.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]SetClassWidgetRepairStation [/b]function creates a link to the user interface class inside the Service Station.
[*] The [b]SetClassWidgetRepairStationStatus [/b]function creates a link to the vehicle status class.
[*] The script subscribes to the [b]RepairEnded [/b]event to receive the player’s exit from the service station event.
[/list]
The player drove into the repair bay, the logic of collecting and generating data for use in further logic chains is triggered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6c486ffe264043cd7aeec42df18d19aa782cb5c6.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]SizeModeWidget [/b]function starts the full access mode to the Service Station functions. Then we display the mouse cursor on the screen (the [b]ShowMouseCursor [/b]variable is responsible for this).
[/list]
Calling the [b]AddDetailList [/b]event triggers a logic chain that forms and sorts car parts into the user interface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/fea687f4af590aa1a99bb9cf3e1c58d415cd8fbb.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/76e1c597340ea1d1ebd3454728f973d617f6d8a9.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Via the [b]ForEachLoop [/b]structure, all values from the [b]PartsList [/b]array are sorted. This is an array that contains a list of all of the car parts.
[*] Then, each part is divided into separate values, which in turn are sent along the required paths to the corresponding variable.
[*] The [b]CreateWidget [/b]function creates an interface element to which the previously received values from the parts list are passed.
[*] Inside the [b]SorterDetailList [/b]function, the received parts are sorted into different functional blocks: “Body,” “Chassis,” “Electrics,” “Engine.”
[*] The [b]SortResourceDetail [/b]function sorts the parts list by their degree of wear.
[*] For further calculations for each specific part, the [b]VehiclePart [/b]variable records data on the name of the part, the degree of its wear, and the duration of repair.
[/list]
Calling the [b]AddDetailImage [/b]event forms a unit of the car status visual display.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/94338ef75885338666b12994a4eae3089cac6194.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Via the [b]ForEachLoop [/b], all the values from the PartsList array are being searched again.
[*] Then, from the data about the part, we get its image via the [b]Break Structure_PartDetail[/b] structure.
[*] Via the [b]addChild [/b]function, a new location is added in the user interface block to which the image is sent.
[*] We get the [b]DetailImageBrush [/b]variable from the created location in the interface block, to which we send the previously received image.
[*] The [b]SetColorDetail [/b]function sets the color of the sent image, depending on its wear and tear.
[/list]
Calling the ActivateModeUI event activates the interaction mode with the Service Station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/81f3ff9a6d32ad597c26886386c6ab94d4145679.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]SetInputModeUIOnly [/b]function sets a condition under which the player can interact only with the user interface.
[*] The [b]StopMovementImmediately [/b]function stops the physical simulation of the player’s car.
[*] The [b]SetViewTargetWithBlend [/b]function changes the player’s surveillance camera. The current camera is turned off and switched to the Service Station camera.
[/list]
The [b]SendDataRepair [/b]event calls the [b]SendingDataRepair [/b]function which sends data about the player, car, and parts to the user interface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c6376f3187316325525c4a554d9b3cec55610dd7.png[/img]

At the current stage, the player can fully interact with the Service Station, see the status of the car, check the integrity of the parts, repair each part separately, select several parts for repair, or repair all worn parts in one click.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e8cddb145f91f6579ed5a1339cf1319c60c04f1b.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]ButtonRepairPressed_Event [/b]event is triggered if the player has pressed the button to select a specific part. In turn, this event triggers the logic of repairing one part. Inside the logic, the selected part is checked and repaired, the wear value is reset.
[*] The [b]PartSelected_Event [/b]event is triggered if the player clicked on a specific part once. The selected part will be recorded in the checklist for subsequent repair.
[*] The [b]ButtonRepairDetails_Event [/b]event is triggered, if the player clicked on the Fix Selected Parts button. This event checks which parts were selected by the player when the PartSelected_Event event is triggered and performs a function similar to the function of repairing one part.
[*] The [b]RepairFullDetails_Event [/b]event is triggered, if the player clicked on the Repair All Parts button. The logic will check all the parts and find those whose resource is below 90 %. Then all these parts are sent to the repair function.
[/list]
After the repair is completed, the player can leave the Service Station. In this case, the script will execute a number of final logics:
[list]
[*] Closes the Service Station mode. The player can no longer interact with the user interface of the Service Station.
[*] Clears temporary variables.
[*] Clears the part lists and parts data.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/fe18b2c59c78e8b456a3c2ff4b9b0e4d586f9505.gif[/img]



[h3]How a Car Wash Works[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c268f721846639f0f72fa0f9fffc6afabb599a7a.png[/img]

The script initialization system at a Car Wash is identical to the rest of the interactive objects. As soon as the player drives up to a Car Wash and presses the interaction confirmation button, the gate opens and the warning lights light up. At this stage, the Car Wash is waiting for the car to get into the washing bay.

We implemented a beam tracing system in the Car Wash instead of animations prepared for each car. This allows you to unify the work logic, regardless of the type and shape of the car. In fact, with this implementation, the logic works correctly with absolutely any object that gets into the washing bay. Invisible beams track the shape of the body and control the movement of all mechanisms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6e9cc94d3f908b9610e3ef0ea59e9e2d2334f2f7.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]EstimationVectorTrace [/b]macro calculates the length of the beam that will track the shape of the car body and also checks the radius of the brush so that the brush geometry does not intersect with the car geometry.
[*] The [b]LineTraceByChannel [/b]function “shoots” a beam to track the point of its intersection with the car body geometry, after which it sends the coordinates in which the intersection occurred further.
[*] The [b]SetWorldLocation [/b]function receives the intersection coordinates and moves the brush to this point.
[/list]
Beam tracing is used in the logic of all movable mechanisms of the washing complex:
[list]
[*] Washing brushes
[*] Washing machine
[*] Drive with washing nozzles
[/list]
Also, at the Car Wash, there is an opportunity to skip the car washing process: for this, we have added the opportunity to drink coffee.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/5423899db3481d9701c4d65f7e17ca2bcfae7f0b.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The [b]ClickedButtonCoffee_Event [/b]event is triggered when the player clicks on the Drink Coffee button.
[*] The [b]DoOnce [/b]operator will execute the logic once, without being able to press the button again during the current washing session.
[*] The [b]CalculateCoffee [/b]macro calculates the possibility of wash skipping.
[*] After receiving approval from the macro, the [b]ForceEnded [/b]event is called, the execution of which starts the process of wash skipping. The screen is darkened, the brushes return to their original position, the washing bay is turned off.
[/list]
After the car wash is completed, the body contamination degree is reset, the gate opens. The player can now continue the game by leaving the washing bay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/14d2c94e37c48365e94b62e760f5183ddbcfc224.gif[/img]



[h3]How the Garage Works[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/0e8f30af9bee5c22453c4a474cef7bab1bbed6a3.png[/img]

The [b]Garage [/b]is the only place where, when entering the zone, the player must complete a full stop [list]
[*] of the vehicle, namely:
[*] activate the hand-brake;
[*] turn off the headlights;
[*] shutdown the engine;
[*] unfasten seat belts.
[/list]
This is implemented as follows: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/9c904400cb23c45391c4884a533b83ed08d58746.png[/img]
[list]
[*] At the entrance to the Garage, the player has a widget with a list of necessary actions. Blueprint gets a link to the car and also checks its initial state.
[*] When a car’s state changes, it transmits via the interface what parameter it has changed and to what value.
[*] After that, the widget marks the new state of the car and checks whether the player has fulfilled all the conditions. 
[*] And if all the conditions are met, the main logic of the garage starts.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/458ac10cdc003eb674a5af1fc319afbeda20d0fa.png[/img]

Here, the player’s car is added to the garage’s array of cars (under the zero index), and the player themselves gets the opportunity to use the garage’s functionality.
[b]Bed[/b]: allows you to rewind time by calling a function in a separate class that controls time at the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f721eb6fa9103c2eebab93f261860ca746f95d2a.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]AddTime [/b]is a function in the LevelTime class that adds time to the current state that the player specified in the widget.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e1587d01f1caf24e0bcc3396dce0d9b36a70038a.png[/img]
In the next issue, we will not talk much and will prepare for you a set of screenshots of the project for the entire time of its development. 

Developer Diaries are published every two weeks. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #4
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4b757f8ad23675c8d9a07f1b7fdac64eb87a6fc8.png[/img]

You will have to continuously assess the traffic situation and constantly make decisions on the road. 
A characteristic feature of the City Car Driving series is the constant monitoring of traffic rules. In CCD 2.0., we make special emphasis on all the accompanying elements of this idea, for example, compliance with the speed limit, the distance between cars, signaling when maneuvering. We have made significant changes to the system for monitoring compliance with the rules, but we do not want to disclose all the details yet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/a03478a042b557a6c8e23d7b93b8dc055777c199.png[/img]

Realistic situations on the road where you interact with traffic will be recreated for you. In early access, we place great emphasis on interaction with all road users.
One of the main changes for City Car Driving is moving away from the fixed weather and time of day, selected before the start of driving, to their dynamic change during driving. Now you will have to take into account the change in road conditions – reduced visibility, changes in grip – adjusting your driving style “on the go,” which will improve your safe driving skills. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/934c8a071f0bd13e2ce94b4e2542cb82461da4f3.png[/img]

Since our game is a simulator, we pay the closest attention to the fact that the controls and the reaction to them correspond to the real ones as much as possible. For example, to start driving a car with a manual transmission, you will need to use the clutch and get used to the range of its “engaging.” 
We try to test our game on all popular input devices and achieve good accuracy and responsiveness of control on each one, so that you can feel like driving a real car.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/d0dc4c00757cfb515cb3cc011ee92b6b64b01d64.png[/img]

One of our main tasks, along with safe driving, is the elaboration of various types of roads: CCD 2.0 provides you with city streets with heavy traffic, highways, roads with turns and intersections suburban area, one-way roads.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f03e9d41ac80f52d66319b56477e2c3751a58c91.png[/img]

We have already shown an urban environment with busy streets and skyscrapers, and now we are creating a forest area: we are paying special attention to vegetation. We added water surfaces, mountains, rocks, bridges, and other objects characteristic of the terrain in which the game takes place. The variety of elements of the environment enriches the game world and makes each location unique.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f1350b1e4718a67f1fbfe1947728d32a2850450e.png[/img]

In addition, we have added various historical and cultural features to the game. Different districts of the city will have their own architectural styles and art objects. This will allow each location to feel in a new way.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/15c454f9619e7c9b4975e8940a89e40546b840fd.png[/img]

Let’s look at the example of one of the locations how the creation of a large city with its own history takes place.
It all starts with a concept, but instead of paper and napkins, we use graphic editors. We start by drawing small sections, which are like puzzle pieces, then we structure and put them together.
If the task is not to reconstruct some real canton of our planet, then at the initial stage, the imagination works mainly. The network of roads, squares, and districts are thrown “out of the head” so that the result corresponds to the meaning of the future location.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/9a687fc90e0070b02994db57b9fb9ffd60820b02.png[/img]

Then, according to the assembled puzzle, a prototype location is created, the so-called “black blokout.” It is black because of the color of the plug objects that symbolize houses and roads in it.
In this “blockout,” changes are made in broad strokes. We look at how the areas of the location are connected, what is the dimension and silhouette of the future city.  
In Unreal Engine, we use BSP geometry to build a location blockout which allows you to easily and quickly set the approximate shape of future houses and the road network.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/eabe7bc93892d1e4e879ca9cc60ca1d1528d1d75.png[/img]

After that, you can think about how the city blocks look like and specify the shape of the road network. So the “black” blokout turns into a “white” one. 
Interactive objects, sights are also installed on the blockout, and routes for the movement of the player, traffic, and pedestrians are laid. 
The stage of the white blockout is considered completed when the level designers, environment artists, and the game designer have a complete understanding of what the location will be and what it will contain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/15067001d33c10811b7c19a49b994da3f9b19f09.png[/img]

After that, the white blockout is transferred to a special editor of the road network and logic in which the final version is built. We had to create that editor ourselves, since no game engine can provide the capabilities we need to model the road network.
Also at this stage, we are considering traffic regulations in the city, defining regulated and unregulated intersections, one-way traffic, lane traffic, main and secondary roads, speed limits, setting road markings, adjusting the intensity and type of traffic, creating a pedestrian network and pedestrian crossings, bus stops and tram tracks.
We can list the amount of work in the road network editor almost indefinitely: from building a general grid of roads to adjusting the height of curbs. 
After setting the logical network, it is necessary to generate its geometry in the editor, which will represent the landscape in the game.
We try to start doing intermediate rough landscape generations as early as possible, since after them, you can see with your own eyes the shape of the landscape, with all the height differences.
After the completion of the main works on the road network, when all the shortcomings have been identified and the landscape artifacts have been corrected, we perform a finishing generation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/bb1b85acbf12b1c2e8e9996ee907e6de839388ca.png[/img]

On the finished landscape, when the final version of the road network is already visible, we proceed to the location design. Level designers together with environmental artists perform architectural filling of the location with large objects. 
At this stage, a visual image of the architecture of the new city is emerging. When all the large objects are placed, interactive objects are installed, when the architecture and style of the city are fully built, the design stage can be considered completed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/dabc1c9c13ac78721e1313dd9e2559a1d5e6bc2a.png[/img]

After that, the final stage begins: we fill the location with objects and traffic regulations, install traffic lights, signs, details of complex markings, and arrows on traffic lanes.
Then we install small objects, for example: fences, poles, benches, and other objects of the urban environment. And then we proceed to the last group of objects – vegetation on the location. After installing all the objects, the location can be “painted” with small details: apply cracks and hatches on roads, garbage, and paving slabs.
This completes the development of the location.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c281d65958c243f8151f28da528a3df99209c552.png[/img]

[b]Will there be trailers in CCD2?[/b] 
[i]There will be no trailers in early access, but we plan to add them after the game is released.[/i]

[b]Will there be trucks and buses available for the player to drive?[/b]
[i]The player will not have large-sized vehicles in early access, but there will be vans; we will tell you more in the diary dedicated to traffic and transport.[/i]

[b]And what about trucks and buses in traffic?[/b]
[i]They will not be available in early access, but we have an alternative, which we will also talk about in the diary dedicated to transport vehicles in the game.[/i]

[b]Will the game physics allow you to perform elements of extreme driving, for example, drift?[/b]
[i]Our project is primarily educational, and we do not encourage extreme driving in urban traffic... But this does not mean that the player’s transport will not be physically capable to do it.[/i]

[b]Are you planning to support telemetry, eye tracking, and so on?[/b]
[i]It is not planned in early access.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/1a8cb6bafe09f9d1bbc1656aa7fa2e9cf454ec24.png[/img]

In the next issue, we will talk about the technical side of the game mechanics, which we mentioned in previous diaries: gasoline station / service station / car wash / garage, and we’ll show you exactly how you can interact with them.

Developer Diaries are published every two weeks. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c190664630e1cce9eb8c943ed60250b566ba30e0.png[/img]

As in the original City Car Driving, you will find a number of useful exercises that will help you master driving at a good level.

In CCD 2.0, the test circuit is designed from the point of view of the sequential passage of all exercises. At the same time, you will be able to independently choose the element that you want to study. 
The test circuit is an important part in the gameplay with somewhat expanded functionality, compared to the original CCD. The following options will be available on the test circuit:
[list]
[*] The ability to perform exercises to hone driving skills with subsequent scoring
[*] Practicing only those exercises in which you are interested, without a scoring system
[*] Going through the entire set of exercises with subsequent scoring
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6ebb95980683a823fd02692de84dd89be8ab91b2.gif[/img]
[i]There are a lot of interactive objects on the test circuit, thanks to them, you will understand when you make a mistake.[/i]

Completing the assigned tasks leads to an exam in the city. For novice drivers, this system will help prepare themselves for full participation in the road traffic.

[b]#1 Hill entrance[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/da1de90cda671c1087317b5da44820360a0c16a6.gif[/img]
[i]At the test circuit, the hill is a high ground with a slope of 12°. According to all the requirements, we have to drive to the highest point, stop, and then carefully move out.[/i]

[b]#2 Cone slalom[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/744f1532cc7eae1666e34218097dc3d976bec4d8.gif[/img]
[i]An exercise in which you need to maneuver along an extremely smooth trajectory without touching the cones. Cone slalom is one of the most interesting classical exercises in preparation for driving in the city.[/i]

[b]#3 U-turn in a restricted space[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/0820629ed87173e85cd45390e32b42bf9f2b7fca.gif[/img]
[i]We are approaching difficult exercises, at this point, you will need to really feel your vehicle.[/i]

[b]#4 Rear entrance to the box[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e024437b3520fbaa0a4b914a941ce16583a0de65.gif[/img]
[i]An exercise fixing maneuvering skills that helps to finally get used to the dimensions of the vehicle.[/i]

[b]#5 Parallel parking[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/7dcdf77df494db71083187a316fe5aab8afb3578.gif[/img]
[i]This exercise is a little test of all your driving skills. For more immersion in the process, there are car mock-ups simulating real road users on the test circuit.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c281d65958c243f8151f28da528a3df99209c552.png[/img]

[b]In addition to exercises, will the emphasis on compliance with traffic rules be maintained in CCD 2.0?[/b] 
[i]Yes, we consider traffic rules to be one of the important components of the gameplay, and we try to deepen the interaction of the player and traffic rules.[/i]

[b]Will the sounds be like in the original CCD or modified?[/b]
[i]With the transition to UE, the sounds in the game will be changed.[/i]

[b]What will happen to the original CCD?[/b]
[i]It will remain with the players, in the form they are used to, we do not replace, and even more so we do not take the game away from people. We do not exclude the possibility of the release of small updates for the original City Car Driving, but now all forces are concentrated on the development of City Car Driving 2.0.[/i]

[b]Is Steam Workshop support planned?[/b]
[i]Yes, it is. We want to give people the opportunity to share their own modifications with maximum convenience.[/i]

[b]Will it be possible to flexibly adjust the traffic density, the number of pedestrians, weather conditions as in the original CCD?[/b]
[i]No, we are trying to give a new experience to all users, so we are trying a different approach.[/i]

[b]Is it planned to introduce motorcycles in CCD 2.0?[/b]
[i]In early access – definitely not.[/i]

[b]Is the system of fatigue, hunger, and so on planned?[/b]
[i]No, we consider this an extra complication for a real and living person who needs to rest and eat themselves, especially when playing a car simulator, where you need to concentrate your attention.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/56ca34bd6f3e28da6287d69f380147de5e830e83.png[/img]
In the next issue, we will talk a little about the game world, show some screenshots of locations, and talk about the approach to level design.

Dev diaries are released every two weeks, where we are talking in detail about the development of the game. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/e3a1aa7336a4b271b30e227f3cd89e98c6cf4c47.png[/img]

When it became clear to us that the original City Car Driving engine was very outdated, we began to look for a new solution that would be:
[list]
[*] Actually developing and interesting for specialists.
[*] Scalable, which would be suitable not only for a new game, but also could be used in the future for our simulators.
[*] Optimized for modern computers.
[/list]
Our search stopped at the Unreal Engine, first of all because of its flexibility in operation and the variability of tools that allow artists and designers to perform many tasks independently. In addition to these reasons, the undoubted advantage of UE is its compatibility with our internal editors: landscape, traffic, and so on.

About a year ago, we created a pilot project on UE4, used internally, after which we transferred all our developments to UE5 in CCD 2.0



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f61727afc3b927fa5754fc0a5804e19b3e0f334d.png[/img]

Let’s start by creating a landscape. The main part of the landscape and roads are created by a generator specially developed by us, which is not part of the UE. Using the same generator, the main AI of urban traffic is created, as well as the logic of pedestrians. As a mandatory feature, traffic control is attached to this. A side part of the landscape is completed by artists as 3D models. With this approach, we can ensure for ourselves a high speed of creating locations with an extensive network of roads and a realistic landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/4b90c4043f359a232c2669198db687b35926b59c.png[/img]
[i]The screenshot shows how the location is filled: objects without textures and detailing are a blockout (a blank for an object). Level designers, when filling the location, work in parallel with viewing the physical properties of the location so that there are no holes or invisible walls. After filling the location, the objects are checked for a collision with the player’s car.[/i]

IWhen filling the location with objects, we use internal developments for automatic placement and generation. In the development process, designers and artists use industry-standard optimization methods:
[list]
[*] Levels of Detail (both manual and automatic).
[*] Geometry Instancing.
[*] Material Instancing.
[*] Combining textures into atlases (both manual combination and automatic when creating HLOD groups).
[/list]
PBR (Physically Based Rendering) materials are used on the objects with the possibility of their customization by level designers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/2764f9d553e7924a7a4e8761c4cba2ae848cabd0.png[/img]
[i]Reflections in the game work on the basis of PBR materials (Roughness-metalness). Thus, materials without roughness have a reflectivity. At the same time, the reflections themselves are generated using SSR (screenspace reflections) technology.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/96e6e2fd9626e2125356e69a6b6b1c123443dbe2.png[/img]
[i]To make the above reflections more realistic, we have added reflections based on HDR (High Dynamic Range) on the car. The reflection capture mode is displayed on the right side of the screenshot. The mode displays the calculation of reflections in real time, this is the main technology that draws reflections on textures.[/i]

At the very beginning of development and at every stage, from the first polygon to the last pixel, we were focused on maximizing the optimization of the game. At the same time, we try to achieve graphics quality that meets the industry standards, adjusted for the chosen style.

UE allowed us to choose one of two types of shading – Forward Rendering or Deferred Rendering. Forward is faster in some cases but makes it impossible to use many effects, reduces the overall performance and quality of dynamic lighting. Thus, in order to maintain the balance of the availability of modern graphic technologies, the speed of work and the capabilities for optimizing the final image, we settled on the Deferred Shading.

Having decided on the type of shading, we moved on to the basic lighting settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/cf3f7b81f9d44bda690f87293afb0f24cc6581c7.png[/img]
[i]It was decided to make the change of the time of day dynamic, so the intensity of the color of the sun and the filling light will be changing. Further, when determining the presence of dynamic light sources (lampposts, illuminated signs, interiors), performance measurement tests were carried out. The measurement results showed that it is necessary to combine different lighting methods – realtime (from light sources in the engine) and baked (glow within the texture).[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/2d2462e90e2c59f3405eb85ad7f381a3da2e66d7.png[/img]
[i]Shadows iare implemented using various UE lights functions and baked shadows at the model level. For example, “cascade shadows” work near the player. The shadow processing mode is shown on the right side of the screenshot. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/915d3e2b4b07702cb80eefcc27ca475820a4713a.png[/img]
[i]At a distance, cascading shadows disappear and DistanceField Shadows, much lighter for the performance, turn on.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/c281d65958c243f8151f28da528a3df99209c552.png[/img]

[b]Will there be different regions, countries, etc. in CCD 2.0? [/b]
[i]In early access, we plan to release only one region: a southern city near the sea, in the future we plan to expand and add game locations.[/i]

[b]In CCD 2.0. will there be an imitation of damages to the car, after which it loses its functionality?  [/b]
[b]It will be, in future diaries we will definitely tell you how we want to implement this functionality. [/b]

[b]Will there be cars from the original CCD in 2.0?[/b] 
[i]No, we want to preserve the uniqueness of the products and will not mix vehicles. There will only be new cars in CCD 2.0.[/i]

[b]Will there be TrackIR support? [/b]
[i]At the moment, support is not being considered. [/i]

[b]Will there be VR support?[/b] 
[i]There will be no support in early access.[/i] 

[b]Will there be an expansion of social interaction with the audience? For example, a discord server, for the opportunity to discuss the game, or to communicate directly with the developers? [/b]
[i]Yes, it will. At the moment, we are preparing a discord server, and as soon as we are ready to launch it, we will immediately inform everyone.[/i]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/6bdba1cb8cb5c34a29d21fdee0c5cb1ac0999f88.png[/img]
For now we have touched only a part of the technologies used. In the following diaries we will tell you more about the graphics.

In the next issue, we will talk about the methodological component in the game and show exercises in the car-racing track. Dev diaries are released every two weeks, where we talk in detail about the development of the game. Don’t miss them!

notes.title: Developers diaries #1
notes.content:
At Forward, we mainly develop [url=https://fwdsim.com]training simulators[/url] and software for them. City Car Driving has been a core gaming product for us for many years. Changing the game engine for City Car Driving 2.0 and creating a project not related to simulators is a big step forward for our small team. We really care about the legacy of the original City Car Driving, making the most of it and trying to add new activities to the game to keep the player engaged at all times


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/f7a30fa3f427787b64fcd2d5f93355b5d40bca12.png[/img]
City Car Driving 2.0 is set in a seaside resort town where it’s always summer.
The main innovation in the game world, compared to the original City Car Driving, is its content. Now all locations, whether it’s a town or suburb, have their own history emphasized by the surroundings.
We have significantly improved the system of occupations and in addition to the updated taxi and transportation of goods, we have introduced several new ones. You can concentrate on a specific job, or do all of them at once, if you like. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44086444/a9e64b14e14fb93a9224653b77fa6d621f61cd90.png[/img]

We are updating City Car Driving mechanics and adding new ones. We’ll be talking about them in our future issues, but for now just take a quick look at them.

[b]Will there be multiplayer? [/b]
[i]We are aware that many of you want to see multiplayer, but at the moment we don’t have the opportunity to fully implement it, while constantly maintaining interest and performance for each player.[/i]

[b]Why is it a new product rather than a development of the original City Car Driving? [/b]
[i]We changed the engine, changed the gameplay, introduced new mechanics, so Car Driving 2.0 is not just a global update – it’s a new game. [/i]

[b]Will players be able to create and add their own cars in City Car Driving 2.0? [/b]
[i]Yes, they will.[/i]

[b]Will players be able to create and add their own maps in City Car Driving 2.0? [/b]
[i]We would really like to provide such an opportunity, especially given that our users would love to create their own maps. However, in the early access version, the map editor is not expected.[/i]

[b]Does your game support gamepad, steering wheel, and other devices? [/b]
[i]Yes, it does.[/i]

[b]Can we get out of the car and walk around the city? [/b]
[i]No, you can’t, at this stage we don’t see any point in creating this mechanic for a car simulator. [/i]
